neighbours.label: a size or timing adjective (early, late, big, huge) after 'a/an' that classifies a person or entity by habit or role ('an early riser', 'a late entrant', 'a big eater')
fire: My uncle has always been a heavy sleeper.
The company was a late arrival in the electric car market.
Their youngest daughter is a huge reader of fantasy novels.
My father was an early adopter of every new gadget.
He became a big supporter of the local football club.
She was a late bloomer who found her talent at forty.
Our dog is a big barker whenever the mail arrives.
The firm was an early investor in solar technology.
quiet: My uncle has always slept heavily on weekends.
The company arrived late in the electric car market.
Their youngest daughter reads huge fantasy novels.
My father bought every new gadget early in the year.
He walked past the big stadium of the local club.
She found her talent late, in a small studio, at forty.
Our dog sleeps in a big basket whenever the mail arrives.
The firm moved early into the solar business park.

notes: card: ' big' x5, ' early' x4, ' late' x4 (an early riser, a late cut, a late entrant, a huge eater, early adopters); + pole is bird and animal species names. Probe: 'was a late addition' 0.76, 'was an early riser' 0.47, 'the big house' 0.02, 'the early morning' 0.15.
